claim: The summary omits that committed refs/heads/main is authoritative and the visible checkout can differ from the graph state the daemon reads.
evidence: The document says 'Graph state lives in a dedicated Git repository' and lists 'The Git-tracked state', mentioning only 'checkout status' locally. src/store/git.rs:110-128 resolves head from refs/heads/main and reads record bytes from that commit's tree, never the working tree. Real consumers use that head: src/transcripts/mod.rs:172-176 builds its CommitView from store.head(); src/transcripts/capture.rs:408-409 loads clone/session state through it. The writer likewise starts mutation from store.head() and Overlay::new at src/writer/mod.rs:277-298, then projects the committed tree to disk at src/writer/mod.rs:400-418. src/writer/worktree.rs:110-121 deliberately leaves differing disk files untouched, records dirty paths at :196-220, and writes view_rev at :221. Thus a listed seat.toml can visibly contain user edits while the daemon still uses its committed contents. This is a material ownership/persistence distinction, rather than an omitted field or layout detail. Additional evidence from the overlapping transactions/recovery review: src/writer/mod.rs:321-340 publishes the main ref before src/writer/mod.rs:387-429 updates SQLite and attempts checkout fast-forward; checkout errors only print a warning and the operation still returns Committed at line 438. Therefore reading or editing displayed files does not necessarily read or change effective graph state.
